aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate cancer; the abstract does not provide staging criteria for advanced disease.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Pre-diagnostic plasma selenium levels were inversely associated with risk of advanced prostate cancer
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the Physicians' Health Study, using baseline plasma from healthy men and 13 years of follow-up
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Using plasma samples obtained in 1982 from healthy men enrolled in the study, we conducted a nested case-control study among 586 men diagnosed with prostate cancer during 13 years of follow-up and 577 control subjects.
reason: The abstract establishes incident prostate cancer follow-up among initially healthy men and separately reports an association with incident advanced prostate cancer. It therefore analyzes both general and aggressive incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Pre-diagnostic plasma selenium levels were inversely associated with risk of advanced prostate cancer (5th versus 1st quintile OR = 0.52, 95% CI = 0.28 to 0.98; P(trend) =.05)
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate explicitly concerns risk of advanced prostate cancer developing during prospective follow-up.

additional_estimates.comparison: 5th versus 1st quintile of pre-diagnostic plasma selenium among case subjects with elevated baseline PSA levels (PSA >4 ng/mL)
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: The inverse association with prostate cancer risk was observed only for case subjects with elevated baseline PSA levels (PSA >4 ng/mL, 5th versus 1st quintile OR = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.28 to 0.86; P(trend) =.002).
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: Incident prostate cancer among men in the elevated baseline PSA subgroup; no aggressive-stage restriction is stated for this estimate.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
